chapter: Louis Armstrong picture, Kid Rena record and Bunk
title: Gilbert's piano and trumpet playing; musicians who loved the music versus money
summary: Rene talks about Gilbert, a friend of his brother who played piano. He then contrasts old musicians who loved playing with today's money-minded ones.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Before you mention Blar and Gilbert, did you know him well?
Well, I know him from playing because him and my brother was pretty good friends. And you know Gilbert could play piano too, you know that? Yeah.
Yeah. Guitar too, now. He plays guitar. Yeah.

And I could play some trumpet, man. Boy, you know, we could call him saying, man, if he had a band behind him, like, he could play, man. Yeah, we played alongside one Sunday, man. He'd say, man. I better kind of feel bad that time too, you see, man. They said, the guy's pumping, man. And Gilbert, and you see Gilbert was just like that. You see. And you've got to be careful when you make something in front of him. Kick it back at you. That's the way he was. He'd catch all that quick, you know. He was just that fast. He had a good head. But I don't know, just some, you know, some of the band, we, I think he'd build up a stronger band after though. Oh, yeah. Yeah, let's see. Yeah. Yeah, I'll tell you one thing, the old days, I don't think they'll ever come back. Because today, now, the fella, you see them old musicians, they played for the lack of an instrument. They loved the music, and they played for the money. But the fellas today, he only wants the money. He don't tell you about how he appreciates his instrument. He don't tell you, man, I sure enjoy playing. All he said, man, they're paying good now. That's all. You get the money. See, go to the job, he play, he won't get off. Soon he get off, he's going to play, and all he wants is the money. But we used to play because we enjoyed the music we played.
